title: 情報工学大意
subtitle: Introduction to Information and Computer Science
keywords: Engineering 2.Manufacturing 3.Regional cooperation 4.Information engineering 5.IT infrastructure/Solutions and Services
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about the connection between engineering and society, as well as the connection between engineering and the local community. (2) learn about the history of those technologies and the technologies of the present and future, and clarify their consciousness in relation to becoming an “engineer who thinks and acts independently”.
advice: This is an introductory course to engineering (Information and Computer Science). We will cover the following materials: 1. Understanding of the College of Engineering: Students are expected to learn and understand the history of the related fields of the College of Engineering, the role and importance of the current and future fields, and the importance of standardization through lectures by teachers and engineers working in society. 2. Understanding of the Department of Information and Computer Science: Students are expected to understand the curriculum in the Department of Information and Computer Science (ICS), the expansion of "areas of study", and their relationship with society. 3. Exercises that foster the ability to think logically about the essence of phenomena and things (scientific skills): Students are expected to understand the role that information engineering has played in society, culture, and history through concrete examples. In order for them to take on such roles, the knowledge and basic skills acquired in the department are important. 4. Introduction of research fields: Students are expected to understand the contents of the "areas of study" in the department of ICS and research efforts in that area. 5. Comprehensive exercises: Students engage in exercises and group activities based on their portfolios and the tasks given in classes to date, and then submit the result as reports to confirm them.
books: Textbooks:Introduction to Computers: Introduction to Information Systems, 8th Edition Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: It is important for students to pay close attention to the technologies they are interested in, and then to tackle those subjects proactively and voluntarily so that they can understand the “areas of study” of the department including the past, present, and future prospects of their research fields. They must also formulate learning objectives and learning plans for future specialized subjects, and determine the direction of their success in their future of society.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the role of the College of Engineering in society and make individualized study plans.
Be able to understand research fields of the department, and consider future study methods and course plans.
Be able to explain the mechanism of a computer and the role of programming.
Be able to explain the role of solutions using information technology.
Be able to explain how services provided by information technology work.
Be able to describe their career development process in their own words and communicate it to third parties.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Be able to understand and explain the interrelationship between other fields of engineering and information engineering. (2) Be able to acquire basic knowledge in a wide range of fields related to information engineering, clarify their learning objectives, study consciousness as future information engineers, and work on studying with enthusiasm.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Be able to understand the interrelationship between information engineering and other fields of engineering. (2) Be able to acquire basic knowledge in a wide range of fields of information engineering, show interest in the usefulness of information engineering, clarify learning objectives and study consciousness, and actively engage in study.

lessons.content: Course introduction Understand learning objectives Manufacturing and engineering Engineering in society.
lessons.assignments: Read the Curriculum Guide Book and this syllabus Understand the learning objectives

lessons.content: International standardization Relationship between manufacturing and international standardization
lessons.assignments: Think about what happens if it is not standardized. Review materials from the last class

lessons.content: Recognize the importance of learning about computers and information systems.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for "Computers and their use" in Chapter 1 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn about the role of information systems in society.
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A (an engineer working in society)
lessons.assignments: Prepare for "Business and Information Systems" in Chapter 2 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn the history of the information field, especially the history of computers, and think about the possibility of future development. Understand how computer-related technology was formed, evolved, and permeated society.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for Chapter 3 of the textbook, "From the Birth of Computers to the Network Society."

lessons.content: Learn about the difference between information, data, and media, how to express data with only 0s and 1s, and how to express numerical data.
lessons.assignments: Preparing and reviewing "Expression of Information" in Chapter 4 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn how to express character data, how to express image data, and how to express voice data.
lessons.assignments: Preparing and reviewing "Expression of Information" in Chapter 4 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn what software is, programming, files and databases.
lessons.assignments: Preliminary study on "Role of Software" in Chapter 6 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn the basics for learning networks, types and characteristics of communication lines, Internet mechanisms and applications, information system processing forms, and corporate information networks.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for "Networks and Information Systems" in Chapter 7 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn how an information system is constructed and maintained along its life cycle.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for "Construction and Maintenance of Information Systems" in Chapter 8 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Learn information ethics when conducting activities using information systems such as computers and networks.
lessons.assignments: Prepare for "Information Ethics and Information Security" in Chapter 9 of the textbook

lessons.content: Review what you have learned so far.
Lecture by external lecturer (Mr. Sasaki) Understand the role of information engineering in the IoT/CPS era.
lessons.assignments: Summarize the content of the lecture and submit it in a report.

lessons.content: Information engineering basic technology and basic knowledge test
lessons.assignments: Thoroughly review and master the basic techniques and basic knowledge learned so far.
Reconfirm the significance of studying at university, future contributions to society, and career development.
